$comment: GOL-2994 — expiring acknowledgements for degraded-skill findings we cannot fix in place.
The normal way to silence a false positive is the `<!-- skill-audit-ignore: path -->`
marker in the skill's own SKILL.md, which keeps the opt-out next to the thing it
describes. That lane is unavailable for a skill installed `editable:false` (vendored
or bundled code): its body cannot be annotated, so a true finding against upstream
would red the weekly audit every Monday forever. A control that cries wolf on a
known, accepted condition is a control people learn to mute.
So: an acknowledgement is an out-of-band, reviewed, EXPIRING record. Rules enforced
- honoured ONLY when the skill is `editable:false`. An editable skill must use the
in-body marker; an entry here for one is REJECTED and the finding still reds.
- past `expires` it stops suppressing and the finding reds again, loudly. Renewing
is a deliberate re-review, not a default.
- every entry needs `issue` and `reason`, so the next reader knows who accepted it.
- the report always prints acknowledged, expired, rejected and stale entries. A
suppression nobody can see is a suppression nobody will revisit.
`expires` is ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, interpreted as end of that UTC day.

acknowledgements.reason: True positive against upstream, not against us: the bundled `paperclip` skill's SKILL.md (line ~130) tells every agent to run this script, and the package does not ship it. The skill is installed `editable:false`, so the body cannot be annotated honest and we cannot add the file. Mitigated for our agents by the company skill `paperclip-board-writes`, which ships a working copy and documents the substitution. Re-review at expiry: if a newer `paperclip` package ships the script, delete this entry; if it still does not, renew and re-escalate upstream.
